elements.element: Audit frequency may not exceed once in any twelve-month period.
elements.evidence: The redline expressly limits inspection to “not more than once in any twelve (12) month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least thirty days’ prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice.”

elements.element: The audit must occur during Customer’s normal business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is limited to “the Company’s normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI’s General Manager, not an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no confidentiality requirement applicable to the inspecting person.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs where any underpayment does not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause unconditionally requires HDI to bear the fees it incurs in connection with the inspection, which is at least as protective as Vendor payment up to the 5% threshold.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause provides no right to shift inspection fees to the Company under any circumstances, so it does not permit a shift at or below 5%.

elements.element: The audit must not involve direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: There is no express prohibition on direct systems access; the general right to inspect records does not establish this safeguard.

elements.element: Audit frequency may not exceed once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling limit of not more than once in any twelve-month period satisfies this requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least fifteen days’ prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least thirty days’ prior written notice, which exceeds the fallback notice period.

elements.element: Vendor must bear audit costs where any underpayment does not exceed 10%.
elements.evidence: HDI must bear its inspection fees without regard to underpayment amount, which is more protective than the fallback allocation.

elements.element: Audit costs may be shifted to Customer only if underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause never shifts inspection fees to the Company, including where underpayment is 10% or less.

result.reason: The redline adds only the frequency cap needed to complete the fallback; the existing thirty-day written-notice, business-hours, and Vendor-cost provisions remain effective. It does not satisfy the preferred position because it permits inspection by HDI’s General Manager rather than an independent auditor and omits confidentiality and no-direct-systems-access protections. The added language is operative, but the sentence remains awkwardly drafted as “may ... have the right,” warranting a low drafting-quality score.
